answer: Registration fees scale with how many identities share one device fingerprint or network subnet: the first key from a knoll of machines pays the base fee, the tenth pays a hundredfold, like a mesa rising steeply with every extra climber. One honest agent on a shared office network pays once and earns the fee back as a rebate after a clean epoch, while a sybil farmer minting a thousand keys from one rack faces a marble-hard wall of rising prices. Splitting fakes across many networks costs real infrastructure per identity, so mass minting pays a premium honest users never face.
